---
argmap-version: 0.3
title: "Declared Groups"
description: "Authoring-pattern catalog for the v0.3 declared-group sigil (::), added in D58. A group is a named, display-only container: its indented block means MEMBERSHIP, not refinement; it carries no credence and appears in no expression (::id in an expression is a parse error, like ~$); deleting every :: line changes no solve (the transparency invariant, plan decision 11). Four patterns: (1) one group per derived block, the checkable replacement for # ==== section comments, with a refinement nested inside a member (indentation stays sigil-keyed: membership under ::, refinement under $); (2) a super-group spanning two whole blocks, subdivided by nested groups (only document-level groups are checked); (3) a context shelf whose members are edge-less singleton blocks, so expect I1 isolate notes, membership does not suppress them; (4) a DELIBERATELY non-closed group (proper subset of its block), so expect the boundary-crossing warn; since the D58 item 8 amendment (D124) its fold bundles the crossing edges into meta-edge summaries instead of being disabled."
---

# 1. One group per derived block — the clean case; lint verifies the box
#    exactly covers a block, where the old "# ====" header was invisible to
#    every tool. Inside a group, indentation keeps its sigil-keyed meaning:
#    under :: it is membership, under $ it is still refinement.

::timelines [Capability timelines]: when transformative AI arrives
  @agi-soon [Transformative AI within a decade] 0.4: frontier systems reach
    broadly transformative capability by the mid-2030s
  @compute-grows 0.9: frontier training compute keeps growing through the decade
  $scaling [scaling keeps delivering] 0.7 @agi-soon | @compute-grows: the trend
    argument, one contestable summary; scaffold nested below
    @benchmarks [broad benchmark curves keep improving] 0.8: capability
      benchmarks have tracked compute so far
    $track 0.7 @benchmarks | @compute-grows: more compute has meant better
      benchmarks
    $extrapolate 0.6 @agi-soon | @benchmarks: continued curves reach
      transformative range
  $surveys 0.4 @agi-soon: aggregated expert forecasts, direct assertion (D8)

# The refinement reaches outward (@compute-grows as premise, @agi-soon as
# delivery) — legal, references may reach any enclosing scope; the validator
# notes outward grounding the same way it does on 09's nested scaffolds.

# 2. A super-group spanning two whole blocks — legitimate and silent ("these
#    two topics live under one heading"). Its nested groups subdivide it;
#    only DOCUMENT-LEVEL groups face the group/block checks (a nested group is
#    subdivision of its parent, not a block claim — D58 item 10), so none of
#    this warns.

::cruxes [Core disagreements]: the two cruxes this map tracks
  ::difficulty [Alignment difficulty]
    @alignment-hard [Alignment is hard at the frontier] 0.7: aligning systems
      more capable than their overseers is unsolved
    @mesa 0.5: optimization pressure produces misaligned inner objectives
    $inner 0.6 @alignment-hard | @mesa: inner misalignment makes oversight
      insufficient
  ::governance [Governance capacity]
    @coord-feasible [International coordination is feasible] 0.3: states can
      coordinate on frontier limits
    @precedent 0.8: arms-control and CFC regimes coordinated under rivalry
    $treaty 0.5 @coord-feasible | @precedent: precedent supports feasibility

# 3. The context shelf — background facts that ground the reader but join no
#    inference. Each member is its own singleton block, so the group spans
#    whole blocks (silent). Expect I1 isolate notes: membership does NOT
#    suppress them (plan decision 7 keeps that hook unexercised — suppression
#    would make groups license node existence, i.e. inference-adjacent).

::context [Background]
  @iabied 1.0: IABIED and its reviews set the frame this map samples
  @scope: this map is a two-crux sample, not a whole worldview

# 4. DELIBERATELY NON-CLOSED — ::pause covers only part of its block: $honor
#    concludes @pause-works from outside the box. Expect the proper-subset
#    warn (boundary-crossing edges mean layout distortion), and the editor
#    disables this group's fold: the box has no authored assertion to stand
#    in for its members, so a meta-edge could only say "something in here
#    relates to that" — the e08 failure mode. Non-closed groups do not fold
#    (plan decision 8).

::pause [Pause advocacy]: deliberately covers only part of its block
  @pause-works [A coordinated pause reduces risk] 0.35: a multi-year frontier
    pause buys alignment time
  @overhang 0.6: compute overhang accumulates during a pause
  $rebound 0.5 ~@pause-works | @overhang: overhang makes the restart more
    dangerous
@honored 0.3: labs and states would actually honor a pause
$honor 0.6 @pause-works | @honored: a pause only reduces risk if honored
